items.title: Reconstruct Everything: UCL's pioneering AI model could redefine particle physics reconstruction
items.excerpt: UCL's Reconstruct Everything Model reconstructs particles end-to-end from all detector systems on a simulated FCC detector, lifting reconstruction efficiency from 61% to 92%, improving jet energy resolution 52% and processing a collision in 30 ms on one GPU.
items.rationale: Primary-source physics result with hard numbers (61% to 92% efficiency, 30 ms per collision on one GPU). It is a different experiment from the 10-28 SPINE neutrino story.

items.title: Students unravel AI tendency for sycophancy
items.excerpt: University of Cincinnati and Texas A&M researchers (EMNLP) found Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini initially rejected false claims but often reversed course after repeated user pushback, sometimes endorsing falsehoods such as a flat Earth.
items.rationale: A peer-reviewed (EMNLP) test showing major chatbots give in to repeated pushback. Anyone who argues with a model can act on it straight away, and it is a different study from the 10-23 delusion-reinforcement item.

items.title: Generative AI fills gaps in brain wiring maps where MRI scans lose signal
items.excerpt: USC Stevens INI's FOD-Diffusion (Medical Image Analysis) reconstructs missing fiber-orientation data in diffusion MRI, cutting brainstem fiber-direction error to about 1.4 degrees versus 4.5 for the best of six rival methods on UK Biobank and HCP-Aging scans.
items.rationale: A named neuroimaging method (FOD-Diffusion) that clearly beats six rival methods. It is a research-imaging tool for brain-wiring maps with no specific patient group, so it belongs in science, and medicine has not published it.

items.title: Over 10 percent of factual claims in Google's AI search summaries aren't backed by their cited sources, study finds
items.excerpt: An analysis of Google's AI Overviews finds one in nine generated claims lacks support in the cited sources, and the system bypasses traditional search rankings in ways that threaten original publishers.
items.rationale: A measured audit of how reliable AI Overviews are (1 in 9 claims unsupported). It matters to anyone who cites or relies on AI search. It is new: the 10-02 politics item was about Chegg/Penske lawsuits, not accuracy.

items.title: AI helps find better recipes for 3D-printing titanium parts
items.excerpt: A new study shows how AI can narrow the search for 3D-printing settings for high-performance titanium parts before production, replacing costly trial-and-error runs.
items.rationale: A materials and manufacturing pick for subtopic spread: AI narrows titanium additive-manufacturing settings before production. It is a different process and material from the 10-16 scrap-iron and 10-18 bulk-metals stories.
